tasks.name: Install full floor protection below ceiling work zone
tasks.notes: Canvas drop cloths or builder's paper over entire floor below ceiling work zone. Overhead spray overspray falls straight down — complete floor coverage required. Significantly more material than wood wall floor protection (full room vs perimeter only).

tasks.name: Install perimeter floor protection at ceiling work zone
tasks.notes: Canvas drop cloth runners along work path below ceiling work area. Brush application has less overspray — drips fall from overhead brush work contained to area directly below worker position.

tasks.name: Mask upper wall band at ceiling-wall junction
tasks.notes: Paper/film + tape masking at ceiling-wall junction to protect finished wall surface from overhead overspray. 12-24 inch masking paper or pre-taped film extending down wall. Spray only. Inverse of wood wall's ceiling_line masking — here we mask the wall BELOW the ceiling.

tasks.name: Mask ceiling-mounted fixtures
tasks.notes: Tape and plastic bag or masking film over each ceiling-mounted fixture (lights, fans, smoke detectors, sprinkler heads). ALWAYS required — fixtures are embedded in the ceiling work surface, unlike wall work where ceiling fixtures are above the work zone. Required for both spray and brush application.

tasks.name: Install lightweight opening covers
tasks.notes: Lightweight plastic pin-up over window and door openings to catch overspray fallout from overhead ceiling spray. Quick pin-up, fast removal. Spray only.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation
sop_modules.notes: Prep tasks vary by substrate type and state. ALL prep work is overhead — significantly more fatiguing than wall prep. Caulk after fill/sand, before primer. MDF edge seal is mandatory for bare MDF.

tasks.name: Dust and clean all wood ceiling surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove construction dust, debris, and surface contamination from all wood ceiling surfaces. Tack cloth or damp wipe. First prep step. Board-style ceilings: clean groove channels thoroughly. ALL work overhead.

tasks.name: Sand wood ceiling per substrate and state
tasks.notes: Bare MDF: 220 grit faces. Bare FJP/softwood: 150-180 grit. Bare hardwood: 150-220 grit. Factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY): scuff sand 150-180 grit. ALL sanding is overhead — pole sander strongly recommended for field areas. Overhead sanding is the most fatiguing prep task.

tasks.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects
tasks.notes: Fill nail/brad holes on boards or panel assemblies. QT3: fill obvious holes. QT4: fill all visible holes. QT5: fill every hole. Board-style ceilings (beadboard, T&G, flat_plank) have high fastener density — each board nailed at every joist. Overhead spackle application is messier — use thicker spackle. Overfill-sand-flush method.

tasks.name: Sand filled areas smooth
tasks.notes: Sand all filled areas flush with 220 grit. QT5: check with angled light for uniformity. Rigid sanding block for flat surfaces (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge for beadboard/T&G grooves. Overhead sanding generates dust that falls onto worker.

tasks.name: Caulk board or beam-panel joints
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at internal joints. Board styles (beadboard, T&G, flat_plank): board-to-board joints. Coffered: beam-to-panel junctions (inside corners) and beam-to-beam joints. Joint density varies by ceiling_style — beadboard has highest density. Use thicker-consistency caulk for overhead work — gravity pulls caulk from joints.

tasks.name: Caulk ceiling-to-wall junction perimeter
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at wood ceiling perimeter: ceiling-to-wall junction (or ceiling-to-crown when crown present). Continuous bead at perimeter where wood ceiling meets adjacent surfaces. LF proportional to ceiling SF.

sop_modules.name: Primer Application
sop_modules.notes: CONDITIONAL — only runs when substrate_state = SS_BARE. Factory-primed substrates skip this module. Primer type driven by substrate. ALL primer work is overhead.

tasks.name: Prime wood ceiling surfaces
tasks.notes: Full primer coat on all wood ceiling surfaces. Spray: broad overhead passes on board faces or panel fields, detail on coffered beam profiles. Brush: work systematically board by board or panel by panel overhead. MDF: step 2 of two-step prime (edges already sealed). Lighter coats overhead to prevent sags.

tasks.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion
tasks.notes: 220 grit light sand entire primed surface. Provides tooth for finish coat. Pole sander for field areas. Flexible sanding sponge for beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel corners. Tack cloth after sanding.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.notes: Finish coat on all wood ceiling surfaces. Material system QT-driven. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). ALL work is overhead — lighter coats to prevent sags. Technique varies by ceiling_style.

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on wood ceiling
tasks.notes: Spray technique varies by ceiling_style: beadboard/T&G/flat_plank — sweep passes following board direction overhead, maintain consistent distance, lighter coats to prevent sags and groove pooling. Coffered — panel fields first (broad overhead passes), then beam faces (partially vertical surfaces with less overhead penalty). Wall masking must be in place. Lead skill for overhead spray control.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on wood ceiling
tasks.notes: Work board by board or panel by panel overhead. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Flat plank: systematic overhead sections. Coffered: panel fields first, then beam faces. Load brush lighter overhead — gravity pulls excess paint. Work in manageable overhead sections to manage fatigue and open time.

sop_modules.name: Between-Coat Interstage
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat
sop_modules.notes: Universal at ALL quality tiers. ALL work is overhead. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3=spot sand only, QT4=full 220 grit, QT5=thorough 220-320 grit. Overhead sanding is especially fatiguing — shorter work intervals may be needed. Rigid sanding block mandatory (FFD §15.4.1).

tasks.name: Clean work area between coats
tasks.notes: Remove dust, debris from floor protection and work area. Sanding dust from overhead work settles on floor protection and surrounding surfaces.

tasks.name: Inspect previous coat
tasks.notes: QT3: quick glance from floor — obvious defects only (overhead inspection inherently less detailed from distance). QT4: systematic scan from step ladder — all visible defects marked. QT5: lighted critical inspection from scaffold/ladder with angled light — zero tolerance. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (beadboard/T&G), beam-panel junction holidays (coffered), sags at board edges.

tasks.name: Sand between coats
tasks.notes: QT3: spot sand nibs/rough spots only. QT4: full 220 grit entire surface. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. ALL sanding is overhead — pole sander recommended for field. Rigid block on flat surfaces (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sponge for beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel corners. Dust falls onto worker.

tasks.name: Patch and repair marked defects
tasks.notes: Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during inspection. Overhead patching — spackle drips. Scope varies by QT.

tasks.name: Spot coat patched areas
tasks.notes: Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat. Overhead application.

tasks.name: Tack cloth all wood ceiling surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat. Cover every SF. Work tack cloth into beadboard/T&G grooves and coffered beam-panel corners. Overhead work.

tasks.name: Final quality inspection
tasks.notes: QT3: scan from floor for obvious defects. QT4: systematic review from step ladder. QT5: critical lighted inspection from scaffold/ladder with angled light. Key checkpoints: groove holidays (beadboard/T&G), beam-panel junction holidays (coffered), sags at board edges, caulk line quality at perimeter, sheen uniformity. Overhead inspection inherently more difficult — angled light essential.

tasks.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
tasks.notes: Correct any remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish. QT5: may require full additional coat if defects are widespread. Overhead touch-up work.

tasks.name: Remove wall upper band masking
tasks.notes: Score tape edge before removal. Pull at 45-degree angle to prevent wall damage or paint peel. Wall_upper_band zone teardown. Spray only.

tasks.name: Remove opening covers
tasks.notes: Remove lightweight plastic from window/door openings. Quick teardown. Spray only.

tasks.name: Remove fixture masking
tasks.notes: Remove tape and plastic from ceiling-mounted fixtures. Always required — setup was always-required. Clean any adhesive residue.

tasks.name: Remove floor protection
tasks.notes: Remove canvas drop cloths or builder's paper from floor. Fold inward to contain debris. More material to remove for spray (full floor) vs brush (perimeter).

tasks.name: Vacuum work area
tasks.notes: Vacuum floor area after protection removal. Overhead sanding generates significant dust that settles on floor.

tasks.name: Clean tools and equipment
tasks.notes: Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products. Solvent cleanup for shellac-based MDF edge sealer residue.

workflow_sequence.standard_bare_spray: MOD_WDCL_SETUP > MOD_WDCL_PREP > MOD_WDCL_PRIME > MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDCL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDCL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_factory_primed_spray: MOD_WDCL_SETUP > MOD_WDCL_PREP > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDCL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDCL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush: MOD_WDCL_SETUP > MOD_WDCL_PREP > [MOD_WDCL_PRIME] > [MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE] > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(1) > MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(2) > MOD_WDCL_INTERSTAGE > MOD_WDCL_FINISH_COAT(3) > MOD_WDCL_FINAL_INSPECT > MOD_WDCL_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.notes: Prime module conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. QT5 brush adds additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle per FFD §15.10.3. Single paintable item (ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL, SF). ALL work is overhead. Height varies per room — estimation engine applies MOD_HT via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND.

round_configurations.name: Primer + 2 finish coats
round_configurations.description: Full coat sequence for bare substrate at QT3/QT4
round_configurations.notes: 3 total coats (1 primer + 2 finish), 2 interstage cycles.

round_configurations.name: 2 finish coats (no primer)
round_configurations.description: Standard coat sequence for factory-primed substrate at QT3/QT4

round_configurations.name: 3 finish coats (QT5 brush)
round_configurations.description: Extended coat sequence for QT5 brush per FFD §15.10.3
round_configurations.notes: 3 total finish coats, 2 interstage cycles. May also include MOD_WDCL_PRIME if SS_BARE.
